topics.label: Course introduction and lecture overview
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the session's focus on the initiation and resolution of inflammation in the context of the course.

topics.label: Innate recognition of infection and damage by pattern recognition receptors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how the innate immune system detects pathogens and tissue damage through molecular patterns, pattern recognition receptor families, and inflammasome signaling.

topics.label: Cellular inflammatory response, leukocyte trafficking, and systemic effects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how sentinel cells initiate inflammation, guide immune cell migration into and out of tissues, and drive systemic complications when overactivated.

topics.label: Resolution of inflammation, tissue repair, and chronic inflammatory states
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover the mechanisms that terminate inflammation, promote tissue repair, and result in chronic inflammation or granuloma formation when tissue homeostasis is not restored.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and next topic
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the lecture and previews the subject of the upcoming lecture.
